report.title: Student Learning Dashboard Human Usability Evaluation Framework
report.research_question: RQ-DASH: Can engineering students navigate concept dependencies, understand latent knowledge estimates, and interpret personalized learning recommendations transparently across Graph and List views?
report.hypothesis: Students achieve >80% task completion on concept localization and recommendation interpretation, with mean Likert transparency ratings >= 3.5/5.0 across both visualization modes.
report.procedure: Structured protocol administering 5 operational tasks (T1-T5) and a 6-item neutral Likert questionnaire (Q01-Q06) evaluating navigation, estimate comprehension, evidence tracing, and Graph vs List views.

report.interpretation: The dashboard usability testing framework is structurally complete and neutral. No human participants have yet been recruited, maintaining zero data fabrication policy. Framework is primed for IRB-approved human validation.
scientific_claims: The dashboard evaluation framework establishes verified schemas, neutral Likert items, and automated aggregation pipelines for human usability studies without data fabrication.
limitations: Actual usability scores require live participant cohorts under approved ethical protocol.
Synthetic benchmark EXP-009 proves interface correctness, but does not substitute for human testing.
No claims regarding student satisfaction or cognitive ergonomics can be made until human evaluation is conducted.
